verdict.rationale: Treasury Prime's own authenticated REST API covers several parts of the story. It lists accounts through the `account` endpoint, returns statements as documents, and exposes status attributes on wire and ACH objects plus card event decline details, so an agent can read the data without scraping a dashboard. An llms.txt file is also published. However, the evidence never shows a unified transaction-history endpoint or an explicit pending-activity view, no MCP server is documented, and the probe found no public OpenAPI spec. missing for 10: explicit transaction-listing endpoint, documented pending/hold activity reads, official MCP server, machine-readable OpenAPI spec, independent hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can read the full banking picture — accounts, transactions, pending activity, documents — through a clean API or MCP surface without screen-scraping a dashboard

citations.quote: Get a list of all the available accounts using the `account` endpoint.
Generate and retrieve branded monthly account statements for your customers.
You can track the progress of a wire by checking the `status` attribute on the Wire Transfer object.
Treasury Prime updates the [ACH object](/reference/ach) status to `returned` and populates the `error` field with the appropriate return code.
Card events in this status will contain a value in the `decline_reason` field which outlines the reason the transaction was declined.
